transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it — totally fair. When she’s at lunch or already on the other line, who answers the calls?
User: Well, we just call people back when Janet's busy or on a break. It's worked so far.
Agent: Makes sense. Where did you first hear about Dialux—was it a voicemail, an ad, or something else?
User: I think it was a voicemail. But really, Janet's been doing a great job for years.
Agent: Oh hey, thanks so much for calling me back! And yeah—sounds like Janet’s solid; when a caller hits voicemail and you call back later, how often do you actually reach them?
User: We never really counted the misses to be honest. It hasn't seemed like a big problem.
Agent: Got it — if you had to guess, on a busy week roughly how many calls end up going to voicemail?
User: If I had to guess, maybe about 15 calls a week during the really busy times.
Agent: Got it — and when you call those 15 back later, do you feel like you’re usually the first one to reach them, or do some of them already book with someone else?
User: Sometimes they've already booked elsewhere, but we do manage to catch a few before they do.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — those “already booked elsewhere” ones are the tough part. What kind of business is this?
User: It's an auto body shop in Boston. We handle repairs, paint jobs, the usual car fixes.
Agent: Got it — auto body in Boston. When those calls come in, are they mostly people wanting an estimate after an accident, or more general repair/paint questions?
User: Mostly people looking for estimates after an accident, but we do get general repair and paint questions too.
Agent: Makes sense—those accident-estimate calls are usually the most time-sensitive. When someone calls for an estimate and you miss them, how quickly do you typically get back to them?
User: Pretty quickly, I'd say, but it depends on how busy we are that day.
Agent: Got it — when it’s slammed, are we talking like within an hour, same day, or sometimes the next day?
User: Usually within the same day, but sometimes it might be the next day if it's really hectic.
Agent: Yeah, that tracks — next-day callbacks are usually where people drift to another shop. When you hear “tell me how this works,” what would you want it to do for you—book the estimate, capture the insurance/claim details, or just make sure no call gets lost?
User: Just making sure no call gets lost would be the main thing, really.
Agent: Got it — mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed calls could be costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead. But like I said, we manage to call people back most of the time.
Agent: Totally—if this is already pretty under control, the math just helps confirm it. Of those calls that go to voicemail, what percentage do you think would actually book an estimate if you answered live—maybe 25%, 50%, 60%?
User: I'd say probably about 50% would book an estimate if we caught them live.
Agent: Got it — and what’s your average ticket value for a typical job that comes from one of those calls (ballpark $400, $650, $850…)?
User: Our average ticket is around $1,100. So, missed calls could add up, but we handle them when we can.
Agent: Makes sense — even if you only save a slice of that, it adds up fast; based on your numbers, that’s about $35,700 a month at risk in the busiest times. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, as a backup layer I can see it. Book your demo for tomorrow.
Agent: Got it — we can do that. What time tomorrow works best for you, morning or afternoon?
User: Afternoon works best for me. How about 2 PM?
Agent: Got it — what time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: I'm in Eastern Time, right here in Boston. So 2 PM Eastern works for me.
Agent: Perfect — and what’s your first name?
User: It's Dave. Looking forward to seeing how this could help us out as a backup.
Agent: Got it, Dave — and what’s your last name?
User: It's Kowalski. Looking forward to seeing how this could support Janet and the team.
Agent: Love that — what’s the name of your auto body shop?
User: It's Kowalski Auto Body. Been here a while, serving the Boston area with repairs and paint jobs.
Agent: Got it — Kowalski Auto Body. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you for the text confirmation?
User: Yes, the number I'm calling from, +16175550005, is the best contact for text confirmation. Thank you.
Agent: Got it, Dave — tomorrow I can do **4:00 PM** or **8:00 PM** Eastern. Which works?
User: Let's go with 4:00 PM Eastern. Looking forward to seeing what you have to offer as a backup.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now. Can you do **8:00 PM Eastern** instead?
User: Sure, no problem. Just let me know once it's confirmed. I'm interested to see how it works.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now. Can you do **11:00 AM Eastern on Thursday** instead?
User: Sounds good. Just let me know once it's all set. Looking forward to seeing the demo.
Agent: Thanks, Dave — we’re having trouble confirming the calendar right now. We’ll reach you at your number within the hour to lock in the time, and I appreciate you taking a look as a backup for Janet and the team. Take care.
